OwnerName: M Hughes, M Kerr-Dineen And Partners
Spotlight: Third in 1m1f Listed race on reappearance and a rallying sixth of 16 in 1m2f handicap at Royal Ascot; drop back to 1m was probably against him on latest start but he's pretty exposed compared to many of today's rivals.

Close second here one year ago; bossed a five-runner handicap at Newmarket (1m2f) impressively this May; doing the same wasn't possible at Royal Ascot, where he wasn't at all discredited in seventh, but he was able to dictate at Newmarket three weeks ago, so what he produced to take 5l fifth of six that day wouldn't cut the mustard in today's race.

Won a maiden at Southwell (1m, AW) in May and pulverised the opposition in a novice at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) in June; 17-2 for handicap debut at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) where he raced freely off the pace and was a never-dangerous eighth, tending to hang up the straight, but that was his best form (beaten about only 4l) and he may be more street-wise this time.

Won novice races at Newbury last October and Windsor (1m2f, good to firm) this June; better form when about 2l fifth of eight on handicap debut at Chester (1m2f, good; 6-1) three weeks ago, close up racing freely early on but keeping on; needs better but could still have potential.

Fair form at Newmarket in his two runs last October; edged out a 1-3 favourite in novice at Lingfield (1m, AW) in May and led over 2f out when easily following up in a five-runner handicap on the turf track there (1m1f, good to firm) five weeks ago; up 9lb and into a much more competitive race but it's hard to pin down exactly how good he is.

Won 1m novice events at Windsor (good to firm) and Nottingham (soft); 9-1, good second of six in a valuable race for handicap debut at Newmarket (1m2f, good to firm) three weeks ago, always close up and racing freely early on; up 2lb but, after just four races, can still do better.

Won last July in his only 2yo start and reappeared with a novice win at Southwell (1m4f, AW) in April; kept to 1m4f when he earned his highest ratings in Listed race at Longchamp and handicap at Royal Ascot (good to firm) last two outings, beaten 8l in both but the way he went last time makes 1m2f look worth a go; yard had two winners at the big Ascot meeting last Saturday.

2yo novice winner and an always-prominent fourth of 30 on handicap debut at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) last month; not so hot at Newmarket (1m) three weeks ago, which sees a tongue-tie enlisted today; his dam being a 1m4f/1m5f winner heightens interest in this new trip.

Won the first of his five races and best form on penultimate start (10.5f, good); 1m4f for handicap debut looked interesting at Royal Ascot (good to firm; 28-1) on latest but he was a never-dangerous 13th of 19 after making a move early in straight, suggesting this trip is a better fit after all.

Contested three 1m maidens on good ground, favourite when coming with a steady run to reel in the front-running Lean d'Aislingean at Ffos Las on latest; this handicap debut is a very different contest, requiring marked improvement, but his dam was a progressive 9.4f-1m4f winner and the best has surely not yet been seen of him.

OwnerName: Hambleton Racing Ltd XXXV & E Burke
Spotlight: Three wins from ten races, the latest win in April on reappearance; well beaten here in May but that was 7f and he's done much better when finishing close up from towards rear over 1m1f at Musselburgh on his two outings since; better is needed but 1m2f looks plausible.

Won a maiden on return and shaped well in a close, running-on fourth on handicap debut next time, both 1m at this track (good); built on that when winning by a nose in 11-runner race at Ascot (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago, when he made up his ground in taking fashion but hung left when challenging; up 6lb but well worth a go at 1m2f and still brings abundant promise.

Solid performances sent handicapping over 1m on his three starts this season, fourth of 11 to Ciarrai Abu at Ascot (good to firm) last time; now 5lb lower than on handicap/seasonal debut, which does not make a compelling case for him but this return to 1m2f is also likely to help.

Set the pace, or ridden up with it, on all three starts; those were over 1m and he was nabbed only late on by Dark Whisper in a maiden at Ffos Las (good; unraced on good to firm) last time; major improvement is needed in this hot race for handicap debut but he's unexposed, with the sire and dam's sire suggesting he will stay.

RaceName: European Breeders Fund EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Hambleton Racing Ltd Xlvii & E Burke
Spotlight: 48,000euros yearling; first foal; dam 5f debut winner (RPR 94), sister to 5f 2yo winner Desert Jungle, half-sister to winners Devonshire (1m Group 2) and Hurryupharriet (5f 2yo Listed), out of multiple 5f winner; represents powerful 2yo yard; this Dandy Man newcomer could have a big part to play.

RaceName: European Breeders Fund EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Disappointing fourth at Catterick (5f, good to firm) last month but prior to that she was a promising second at 28-1 in the Hilary Needler at Beverley (5f, good to firm) on debut, and she sets a good standard if rediscovering that form.

Similar standard of form in 6f maiden at the Curragh (good) on debut and when fifth at Fairyhouse (6f, good); mid-field at Navan on third start; reacted well to the addition of cheekpieces when a narrow winner from Seven Nation Army in a 6f nursery at the Curragh; good 7lb claimer counters 7lb rise.
Showed little on his first two starts; was able to dictate in a 6f Fairyhouse maiden and gave a much-improved display to take second; opening mark looks quite stiff.

OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: Has been running over shorter distances; best run when second over 5f at Bellewstown; tame effort over the same trip at the Curragh last time; may improve over this trip; rider's claim an asset.

Given three runs in nine days in May to get a handicap mark; none of his efforts was particularly notable; gelded before bringing an intriguing profile to his first handicap at the Curragh; ran a bit green when fighting out the finish and lost out narrowly to I Ready; trip should suit, may cope with extra 5lb.
Improved from her Leopardstown debut on soft to win a 1m Bellewstown maiden on good ground; opening mark seems fair enough, getting weight from four maidens.
Limited appeal on maiden form; first time with cheekpieces; Seven Nation Army appears to give the yard a better chance.
Has shown little in maidens; in receipt of plenty of weight from his seven rivals; however, he is 3lb out of the handicap.

Improved for the step up to 6f when runner-up at 40-1 in the Coventry at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm) and bumped into an exciting Godolphin winner when second of three in the Group 2 July Stakes at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; there's every chance he'll be in the mix.

Won on debut at Newcastle (6f, AW) before finding the drop to 5f against him at Beverley, and he was back on the scoresheet in a 6f nursery at York (6f, good to firm) last time; it was a Class 4 contest on the Knavesmire and this is considerably tougher, but he did it comfortably and the clear runner-up has won since; not ruled out each-way.

Impressive on debut at York's Dante meeting (5f, good) and confirmed that promise with close fourth in the Coventry at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm; Adaay Of Scarlett second); open to further improvement and he's firmly in calculations for a stable that has enjoyed plenty of success in this race.

OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: Won on debut at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month and again had plenty in hand when streaking clear to follow up in a conditions race at Ascot (6f, good to firm); his stable won this in 2023 and he's an exciting prospect who could take today's rise in grade in his stride.

Made it 2-4 when making all in the Woodcote conditions stakes at Epsom (6f, good to soft) on Oaks day; another good run when third of three in the Group 2 July Stakes at Newmarket three weeks ago (6f, good to firm; Adaay Of Scarlett second) but it's likely his limitations will again be exposed.

Placed on first three starts (5f, good/good to firm) before respectable ninth in the Coventry at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm); showed blistering pace when easily making all in first-time cheekpieces in a recent maiden at Ffos Las (6f, good) and he could have more to offer in the headgear; interesting contender for trainer who has won three of the last seven runnings.

OwnerName: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg
Spotlight: Improved upon his debut fourth at the Curragh (6f, good) in June when coming clear late on in a big-field maiden at Naas (6f, good) last Wednesday; others have more substance to their form but he's the sole Ballydoyle representative and could have lots more left in the tank.

Unplaced on his three outings since winning at Leicester (5f, good to firm) in April on his second start, but he kept on nicely in a first-time visor (retained) when seventh of 21 in the Norfolk at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) last month, and he could outrun his forecast big odds back up to 6f.

Won over 6f on first two starts (a conditions race here on the second occasion) before close fifth in the Coventry at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm) behind Adaay Of Scarlett and Cut A Dash; could be bang there.

Beat Hickory Lad to win for Kevin Ryan on debut at Thirsk (5f, good) and had subsequent Royal Ascot runner-up Adaay Of Scarlett in second when a Listed winner at Sandown (5f, good) in May; merely mid-division in the Norfolk at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) but he's better than that and it's possible the step up in trip will suit on his stable debut; not written off.

Sole win from 13 starts came in a Ripon novice over 1m in 2024; best effort this term came when third of 11 over this C&D in May but he's been down the field on his last three starts; tongue-tie added.
Often slowly away, just as he was when winning at Doncaster (1m, good to firm; first-time tongue-tie) last week having dropped a long way in the weights; has to be respected under a 5lb penalty.

Nine-time winner whose best effort this year came when a close-up third over C&D in May, taking his form figures at this track to 213; below his best in two starts since and has left the Newland-Insole stable (bought for 9,000gns); visor replaces blinkers for his yard debut and he's interesting.
Gained his second win on turf when landing a Doncaster handicap under Elle-May Croot 12 days ago, bouncing back from a lesser effort; can't be dismissed off this 4lb higher mark.
Runner-up in two novice/maiden events last year but she's failed to beat a rival home in each of her last three starts, including two handicaps this year; lots to prove.

RaceName: Arthur Guinness Irish EBF Corrib Fillies Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: J P Magnier/Mrs P Shanahan/Mrs M V Magnier/K MacLennan
Spotlight: Ran nine times for Ollie Sangster, winning twice as a 2yo, also Listed-placed last season; excellent debut for this stable when winning Group 3 at the Curragh in April (1m, soft-to-heavy); backed up that run in less testing conditions when beaten 3l into seventh in Group 2; now has to bounce back from a disappointing Leopardstown run; cheekpieces on.

RaceName: Arthur Guinness Irish EBF Corrib Fillies Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Good maiden for this stable at two, made the frame on all four starts, notably when third in the Goffs Million and fourth (demoted from third) in a 1m fillies' Group 3 event; placed in three of her four starts for Brendan Walsh in the US; had a confidence-boosting win against much inferior opposition at Killarney.

RaceName: Arthur Guinness Irish EBF Corrib Fillies Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won a Dieppe maiden (1m3f, heavy) just over a year ago; not seen again until well held on her stable debut in the Kensington Palace at Ascot (1m, good to firm); decent effort when fifth at 33-1 in a Listed race at Pontefract; aiming high again here.

RaceName: Arthur Guinness Irish EBF Corrib Fillies Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: K Blake/Mrs E Palmer/M Wilson/N Luck
Spotlight: No further success since debut win for Karl Burke at York two years ago; denied three times by the useful Rion Rubette in handicaps at Gowran this season; not one of her better runs at the Curragh last time; lowest-rated filly in the field.

RaceName: Arthur Guinness Irish EBF Corrib Fillies Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: Mrs R G Hillen And Partner
Spotlight: Lightly raced French winner (1m, soft); bright start for her new connections when runner-up in a Group 3 at Lingfield (7f, good to firm) in May; not in the same form when fourth in a Listed race at Musselburgh (7f, good) in June.

RaceName: Arthur Guinness Irish EBF Corrib Fillies Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won a 2yo maiden on debut for Jessica Harrington; ran some good races in defeat last year; joined Johnny Murtagh this term; fair fourth behind Meriden at the Curragh in June; did well to finish third of six in a 7f Group 3 race at Leopardstown; however, that looked a sub-standard affair, and she may be flattered by the resultant 12lb rise to a mark of 95.

RaceName: Arthur Guinness Irish EBF Corrib Fillies Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won races over 1m at Naas and Navan last August; final two 2025 starts in Listed races were ambitious; never in the hunt in the Irish Lincoln on reappearance; no luck in running at Limerick last time; stiff task in this grade.

RaceName: Arthur Guinness Irish EBF Corrib Fillies Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Group 3 winner at the Curragh (7f, soft) last September and runner-up in the same grade there (1m, good) in May; fourth in the Irish 1,000 Guineas at the Curragh (1m, good), beaten around 6l; sights lowered considerably now after ambitious Coronation Stakes run; new headgear combination.

RaceName: Arthur Guinness Irish EBF Corrib Fillies Stakes (Listed Race)
OwnerName: Patrick John O'Brien & Mrs Paul Shanahan
Spotlight: One of the stars of the season; started a five-race winning sequence by scoring off 57 at Ballinrobe two months ago; now an astonishing 46lb higher after four handicap wins (including a fillies' premier contest at the Curragh) and a Killarney Listed success at the main expense of Royal Ascot handicap winner Green Carrera; tough, ground-versatile; stiff 7f should suit.

RaceName: Arthur Guinness Irish EBF Corrib Fillies Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won a C&D maiden in good style last year; has run well in defeat in Pattern company over this trip, second to Black Caviar Gold last autumn, and third (behind True Love) at Leopardstown in April; last two runs have been in 1m races, held by Black Caviar Gold on Irish 1,000 Guineas running and has a 3 1/2l to find with Meriden on Killarney running.

Ran in two Group 2s as 2yo and progressive at Listed/Group 3 levels this season, winning well at Leopardstown (1m1f, good) two weeks ago when he reverted to front-running; probably stayed 1m2f on penultimate start, without shouting that he's a 1m4f horse.

Pushed Maltese Cross all the way in Lingfield Derby Trial (11.6f, good to firm) and, although losing ground on that rival, fourth in the Derby at Epsom (1m4f, soft) was creditable; however, needs to bounce back from the German Derby (1m4f, soft) in which he was favourite but tailed off.

Won a good duel for maiden at Cork (10.5f, good to yielding) in April and followed up in a 19-runner race for handicap debut at Royal Ascot (1m4f, good to firm) six weeks ago, challenging entering the straight and tenaciously keeping the rest at bay; no harm for the Ascot form that the second hacked up last Friday and the third was a close third in Listed race; scopey sort who looks open to further improvement and should be a leading player.

Can make the running; won two 1m4f handicaps and so nearly got back up over 1m6f at Newmarket on latest start; no show, however, when he tried a 1m6f Group 3 at Royal Ascot (100-1) and he is bottom of this pack on ratings.

Useful form in defeat, coming from the back, on all starts this season; best form when losing out narrowly in the London Gold Cup at Newbury (1m2f, good) before he never threatened when cheekpieces went on at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm; 6-1); gelded since; while 1m4f may now be worth a go (he's not really bred for it) he needs improvement on this move from handicaps.

Sole win from seven races was a 1m2f maiden in March but he's also contested four Group events; best form when third in the Group 3 Gallinule at the Curragh (1m2f, good; unraced on firmer) in May, before weakening to a 13l defeat when fifth there in the Irish Derby (1m4f); that leaves his stamina unproven but his dam was suited by the trip.

OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: Second in the Group 1 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket last October (good) and returned there with a fine third in the 1,000 Guineas (good to firm); tailed-off last, however, in the Oaks at Epsom (1m4f, testing ground) and the Group 1 Falmouth at Newmarket (1m, good to firm); while bred to stay at least 1m2f, she now has a big question to answer.

RaceName: Download The Oddschecker App Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won a Leicester maiden (6f, soft) last October but he was gelded after a disappointing comeback at Newbury in April; ran into some trouble when a respectable fourth at Sandown in June but he failed to build on that at Ascot (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago; still unexposed after only six starts but he needs improvement at this new trip.

RaceName: Download The Oddschecker App Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won four times on the Flat when based in France, with first three on AW and latest on good to soft; hasn't been with David Pipe for long but she was well held at Salisbury (1m2f, soft) last month and it was the same story on her hurdling debut at Newton Abbot (second of three) last time; others preferred.

RaceName: Download The Oddschecker App Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won on debut at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) in December but he's been well held in three subsequent runs including two handicaps (1m2f, good to firm); still early days but he needs to raise his game to make an impact.

RaceName: Download The Oddschecker App Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Mixed form in three novice/maiden events but he started his handicap career with a rallying fourth at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago; looks interesting now upped to this trip and he's a half-brother to some useful winners.

RaceName: Download The Oddschecker App Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Improved on her debut form when winning at Lingfield (1m, AW) in December and she took another major step forward when making all to beat a subsequent winner at Bath (1m2f, good to firm) in May; returns after another break but that was a comfortable success last time and she's open to more progress on handicap debut; big player.

RaceName: Guinness Open Gate Brewery Novice Chase (Grade 3)
Spotlight: Smart hurdler won four races in that sphere including in Listed company last year; pulled-up in a Grade 1 Aintree novice on return in April; quickly rebounded with a Limerick novice chase win over Le Coq Hardi and followed up at Killarney; already  looks a better chaser and respected despite a double penalty.

RaceName: Guinness Open Gate Brewery Novice Chase (Grade 3)
Spotlight: Clonmel maiden hurdle winner over this trip last year and rated 111 in that sphere; point winner took his form to a new level with a decisive chase debut win at Down Royal; this is tougher but can be involved.

RaceName: Guinness Open Gate Brewery Novice Chase (Grade 3)
Spotlight: Dual hurdle winner over shorter and has already had eight chase runs; beaten 12l by Shadow Paddy on return at Limerick but went one better at Kilbeggan since; cheekpieces added and needs more.

RaceName: Guinness Open Gate Brewery Novice Chase (Grade 3)
Spotlight: Maiden hurdle winner is rated 130 in that sphere but lost his form after some poor jumping; didn't jump well when won on chase debut at Wexford either but can surely do better with that experience behind him.

RaceName: Guinness Open Gate Brewery Novice Chase (Grade 3)
Spotlight: Useful hurdler in France has won 2-3 over fences for this yard; won well at Wexford before disappointing there; however, was impressive at Roscommon next time; that was all over 2m but can be a big player if staying this trip.

RaceName: Guinness Open Gate Brewery Novice Chase (Grade 3)
Spotlight: Rated 105 over hurdles but performed above that level when winning on chase debut at Wexford, jumping well; however, this is much tougher and a place looks the best she can do.

RaceName: Guinness Open Gate Brewery Novice Chase (Grade 3)
Spotlight: Rated 120 over hurdles with four wins to her name; was a ready winner on chase bow last time at Wexford; this is tougher but gets plenty of weight and can be a player.

Won the Group 1 Prix de l'Opera at Longchamp (1m2f, very soft) in October 2024; stepped in a hidden drainage hole and pulled up at Haydock this May when returning from a very long absence, but looked as good as ever when third in the Group 2 Duke of Cambridge Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) last month, staying on well having been denied a clear run; could play a leading role back up in trip.

Beaten just a neck in this race in 2024 (good to firm) and heavy ground was against her when a below-par third 12 months ago; won the Group 2 Middleton Stakes at York (1m2f, good) this May for the second year running; well beaten in the Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot last month and now 0-13 in Group 1 races, but she's still entitled to respect back against her own sex.

2-2 prior to keeping on well for third in 1m Listed race at York (good) in May and she improved for the step up to 1m2f to win the Group 3 Hoppings Stakes by a short head at Newcastle (AW) last month, coming clear with a classy Godolphin 5yo; others have stronger form but she's unexposed and well worth a crack at a Group 1; could give a good account.

OwnerName: M Tabor & D Smith & Mrs J Magnier & Westerberg
Spotlight: Her 5-5 record includes French Group 1 wins on her last three starts, with this season's coming in the Poule d'Essai Des Pouliches at Longchamp (1m, heavy) and the Prix de Diane at Chantilly (10.5f, good to firm); it was a very tight finish last time but she's clearly a top performer and her trainer has won this with 3yos six times, including the last two runnings; leading claims.

OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Group 3 runner-up at the Curragh last August but unplaced on her four runs since and it's likely she'll assume a pacemaking role for stablemate Diamond Necklace, as was the case in the Prix de Diane last time.

RaceName: Get Best Odds With Oddschecker EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands B, C & D) (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Julie Martin & David R Martin & Partner
Spotlight: Progressive form in his first three runs culminating in a near-miss in a Wolverhampton maiden (8.6f, AW) last month; flopped on handicap debut at Ffos Las (1m2f; last of five) but may have had stamina issues and he sets a good standard on this drop back in trip; key player back in a novice.

RaceName: Get Best Odds With Oddschecker EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands B, C & D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Victor Ludorum gelding; beaten 6l when runner-up at Hamilton (8.3f, good to firm) two weeks ago but that was behind a 2-13 shot and he pulled clear of the third; should know more this time and has possibilities if he can build on that debut effort.

RaceName: Get Best Odds With Oddschecker EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands B, C & D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Weak 14-1 shot and he finished a remote sixth of nine on recent Wolverhampton debut (7f, AW).

RaceName: Get Best Odds With Oddschecker EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands B, C & D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 36,000euros 2yo; fifth foal; half-brother to winners Sayulita (German 1m2f), Idalita (French 1m5f/14.5f) and Cefalu (US 8.5f turf); dam French 1m winner, half-sister to winners Salve Venezia (German 1m2f Listed) and Sun Of Gold (French 1m6f Listed); yard is in good form and he needs watching in market on debut.

RaceName: Get Best Odds With Oddschecker EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Horses In Bands B, C & D) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Gleneagles filly who is out of an unraced half-sister to 1m4f Group 2 winner Pongee; well-held second when odds-on for Ripon debut (1m, good) this month but she ran well for a long and was 8l clear of the third; should improve for that experience and she's respected.
Has shown improved form lately, winning a maiden and two novices in the UK recently; however, this is much tougher giving away weight to all; looks yard's second-string.

Bumper winner on debut for Sam Curling last year; didn't go on initially over hurdles for this yard but better this year, winning a Fairyhouse maiden and Killarney novice over this trip; is a leading player.

Point runner-up was second in a maiden hurdle on rules debut before a lesser bumper run; was happier back over obstacles when winning a 2m3f Punchestown maiden hurdle last time; has to do more but is improving; tongue-tie on.
By a top French sire but unsold for 25,000euros as a 3yo; looked green so did well to win a 2m2f Kilbeggan maiden hurdle on debut; this is way tougher but can't be dismissed either.
Flat maiden easily got off the mark at Downpatrick over 2m2f on 15th hurdle run; however, this is way tougher and he will need another step forward.

Placed over hurdles in France and some decent efforts initially in defeat for this yard including in Martin Pipe at Cheltenham;  easily won an uncompetitive Downpatrick maiden last time; solid chance.
Some decent bumper form for Lorna Fowler without winning; an improved effort to get off the mark in a 2m Punchestown maiden last time; up in trip and this is way tougher.

Showed some promise in bumpers without looking like a winner-in-waiting; however, was much-improved to run away with a Limerick maiden over this trip on hurdling debut; more to come and can be in the mix.

In fine form over 5f and although he paid a high handicapping price for a wide-margin Redcar win in June, he so nearly overcame the 8lb rise at York next time against Naana's Shadow; had more to do at Ascot (good to firm) after but produced another sterling effort in a close sixth of 15; solid claims back against his own age group.

Front-running winner of two AW races for this yard, at 6f and 5f; 0-9 on turf but he had big tasks either side of a break and he's likely to find this sharp test more to his liking than the one at Pontefract 13 days ago, when he was headed only near the line; likely to give a punchy show.

Has won three of four 5f turf handicaps for this yard, including the 3yo Dash at Epsom and a narrow defeat of Schrodinger's Cat at York in June; has since done well in a Listed race there (good to firm) considering the tough task she faced at the weights; has good chance back in a handicap.

Bright start to career when justifying short odds at Doncaster (5f, good to firm) in April and, after two defeats in Listed races, he made some late headway into third, beaten nearly 3l, behind Naana's Shadow and Schrodinger's Cat on handicap debut at York (5f, good); lacks experience generally and also of a downhill track but he has potential.

All three wins over 5f on sharp tracks, most recently when making all at Thirsk (good) in May; found out by Ascot's stiffer test and tough company at the Royal meeting in June and needs another push to win off her current mark.

Two 5f wins for other yards in a Catterick novice as 2yo and a Meydan handicap in January; along with 25 others she was outclassed by a handicap blot at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm) on yard debut but less than 2l covered the second and seventh (where she finished; raced without a shoe) and there could be better to come for her leading trainer.

Often leads; won first two juvenile starts (extended 5f and 6f); placed only once in three 6f starts this year but he remains capable of better and, following a flagging fifth of 13 at Newmarket recently, he's worth a look in this first attempt over a bare 5f for yard that won this in 2021.

Progressive 3yo who has moved on from her opening 5f wins on the AW with a good third of 16 to Naana's Shadow in the 3yo Dash at Epsom in June then setting a strong pace in an Ayr Listed race (5f, soft) when hanging on for fifth; goes without aids for the first time and is 5lb higher back in a handicap but she may well continue to go the right way.

All races at about 6f, looking likely to find his feet at an even better level when beating a fair type at Windsor (good to firm) in June; lost his chance at the start at Newmarket since and remains one to be interested in; however, this very quick 5f may be an eye-opener for him.

Sole win in 5f 2yo conditions race at Beverley (good) and later a good third in 6f handicap at this meeting (good to soft); never best placed after a slow start on Sandown comeback when better than the bare result in sixth but he was withdrawn after getting upset in the stalls in May and his chance is likely to depend on what happens before the race starts in earnest.

On the go since his debut last August but never better than of late, making all over this C&D in June and scraping home at Sandown (good) since; needs to find further new reserves after another 3lb rise.

Has proved ideally suited by 5f on good to firm and, despite taking a hefty rise for two June wins, he didn't take much urging to get to the front at Newmarket last time, before nudged out to hold the second; a further 5lb rise in a better race asks for more but he should be in contention; yard won this in 2019.

Won at both sprint trips as a 2yo but he hasn't been at the forefront of calculations in three turf handicaps this year and has ground to make up on Quantum Power on their recent Newmarket run; looks to have his share of weight and fitting a tongue-tie needs to make a difference.

Followed a Bath maiden win (firm) with an impressive return to handicap company at Haydock (5f, good to soft) in May; saddle slipped when down the field later that month and he's been gelded since; 7lb higher mark than at Haydock may not be too much to ask and he's one of the more interesting ones.

Capable of much better than she showed on good to soft ground at Hamilton six weeks ago, such as when dashing home, after finally getting a clear run, to divide Naana's Shadow and Shes Got A Brother in the 3yo Dash at Epsom (good); no surprise to see her revive back on more suitable ground.

Off the mark on turf when wide-margin winner at Yarmouth (5f, soft) in May and he did well to finish within 2l of Naana's Shadow in the 3yo Dash at Epsom next time as he took a while to pick up; two lesser efforts have followed, though, and he looks vulnerable.

Added to an earlier Windsor win when beating three rivals at Nottingham (5f, good to firm) last week; ran respectably in a less competitive C&D race than this in May but a tendency to get behind early is a worry in this big field and he's 3lb badly in under a penalty.

Has come into his own in 5f handicaps for this yard, looking ahead of his mark when winning cosily at Newbury (good to firm) latest, despite hanging away from the whip; has a much stiffer task in this company but his dam won this race for the stable in 2020 when wearing first-time cheekpieces, as her son does today; just out of the weights but intriguing.

Reeled off four straight hurdle wins last summer before losing his way; minor form when qualifying for a mark on the Flat since but he's proved well ahead of it since handicapping with cheekpieces refitted, winning by 6l at Thirsk (1m4f) and Lingfield (1m6f; both good to firm); 3lb well in under big penalty; major claims.

Had placed form at 1m4f and 1m7f in France; 2-13 over hurdles for this yard but she hasn't looked well treated since her March win and wasn't at her best three weeks ago; her Flat mark doesn't look anything special either.

Well treated on the form of his two 2m wins (good to firm and good) in 2025 and although he hasn't been himself this year, the signs were better when he was second of five on this course (2m2f) two weeks ago; has another well-treated rival to contend with today but he should be competitive.

OwnerName: Mrs E Bickerton And A Streeter
Spotlight: Turf wins at 1m6f (good to soft) and 2m (good); quite well treated now and his AW reappearance was encouraging but he didn't fare so well back on turf in June and it's two years since he was risked on good to firm ground.

Three-time Grade 1-winning chaser who has counted Gaelic Warrior and Marine Nationale among his victims in top-level races; winner of two of his six races over hurdles, one in France at four, the other a three-runner Sligo contest two years ago; warmed up for this with a run on the Flat at the Curragh 11 days ago.

Highly creditable third behind Ndaawi here 12 months ago before winning a big 2m handicap at Listowel; faced a straightforward task in a three-runner contest at Down Royal before running well up to the point of his fall at the last in the 2m4f Hatton's Grace; fair third behind Lossiemouth at Leopardstown's Christmas meeting; 14lb higher than last year.

Promoted winner of this race last year after receiving critical interference; has been mixing hurdling and Flat action since then, down the field in the County Hurdle; beat the very useful Absurde in a conditions' hurdle at Cork in April; kept ticking over with an odds-on Flat win in a 1m6f Listowel contest two months ago; 7lb higher than last year.

Smart bumper form; fell with race at his mercy on hurdles debut at Leopardstown in December; survived a final flight blunder to win a maiden at Thurles; best of the Irish in the Supreme Novices', though no threat from the last; faded quite tamely in Grade 1 at Punchestown; retains a good reputation and has been a leading ante-post fancy.

Useful three-time Flat winner for William Haggas; has developed into a smart handicap hurdler; stuck to his task when first past the post in a big field at Aintree's Grand National meeting (2m, good to soft) only to be disqualified for a whip offence; 6lb extra for that arguably made the difference when he was beaten a neck in the Swinton at Haydock; progressive sort.

Won 4yo handicap hurdle at 2025 Cheltenham Festival and had a massive payday in last season's Irish Cesarewitch; down the field in three big handicap hurdles between late November and April; not much luck when unplaced favourite for the Chester Cup; flopped when well-fancied for the Ascot Stakes; questions to answer but could not be ruled out.

Did well to win a conditions event on the Flat at Fairyhouse this month on his first 2026 outing; fair fifth in Monday's big amateur race (one place in front of stablemate Too Bossy For Us); first hurdles run since fourth in this last year; could go well if recovered from Monday's race.

Grade 1 juvenile winner at Aintree (2m1f, gd-sft) in April 2025; best run last season when fourth at Leopardstown in February; struggled in valuable handicaps at three festivals, with soft ground probably to blame; regained the winning thread in mares' race at Listowel in May; beaten favourite for a similar race at Killarney; Paul Townend's choice, has to be taken seriously.
Struggled in top company after a maiden win at Punchestown in February; one place behind Tounsivator when sixth in the amateur handicap on Monday.

OwnerName: Mrs Caroline Hendron & Mrs M Cahill
Spotlight: Enjoyed a career highlight when winning the Group 1 Tattersalls Gold Cup in 2021; very nearly matched that achievement when first-past-the-post in this race last year, demoted for causing interference to Ndaawi; no sign of that standard of form in valuable handicap over hurdles or on the Flat since then; still 5lb higher than 12 months ago.
Promise in bumpers without winning; highly tried after winning a maiden hurdle at Limerick last Christmas; seventh in a 12-runner Grade 1 at the DRF, fifth of six in a similar race at Aintree.

Impressive winner of a Ballinrobe bumper for Andrew Slattery a year ago; won a Punchestown maiden hurdle last October on stable debut before finishing fourth in a Fairyhouse Grade 2 novice; third in a conditions event at the Punchestown festival; outstayed by an emphatic winner on handicap debut in a 2m4f contest at Kilbeggan.

Opened his account off a modest mark of 94 in a C&D handicap hurdle in October 2024; has now obtained a rating of 132 after recording his fourth handicap success at Killarney in May; seldom runs a bad race and was placed twice at last year's festival, third in the big amateur handicap and second in a handicap hurdle.

Fair fifth in a valuable handicap hurdle at the Punchestown festival; a shade disappointing at Listowel in June before making amends at Bellewstown; may continue on the upgrade for Tony Martin who has won this race four times in the past 12 years.

Flat maiden in France; made a couple of mistakes when winning a maiden hurdle at Limerick in March on his second run for Willie Mullins; again untidy at times when coping well with a marked step up in class to win a Punchestown festival conditions race; no match for a 10lb-receiving rival at Bellewstown; winner was trounced by a Mullins novice here on Monday.

Won a maiden at Wexford on debut last October; next two races were highly ambitious, in the Royal Bond and the Supreme Novices'; struggled in a Cork conditions race won by Ndaawi; addition of a tongue-tie did the trick when he gained a second Wexford win in May.

Three hurdle wins and six seconds, including a pleasing effort behind Murcia at Listowel in May; has run twice on the Flat since then, went close in a handicap at Ballinrobe, out of the money behind Tounsivator at Fairyhouse.

Useful on the Flat for John Murphy, 2-4 and rated 101; failed to prosper as a juvenile hurdler for this stable after a winning introduction at Navan last November; completely tailed off in the Fred Winter; in rear in the Bellewstown race won by Putapoundinthejar.

Won on the Flat in France (soft); looked promising when winning a 4yo maiden hurdle at Naas in January (2m, heavy); major doubts raised by his last four runs; pulled up in the Triumph; beaten when unseating at Fairyhouse; dropped away in Punchestown Grade 1; disappointing at Ballinrobe; beaten 8l in the big Flat handicap here on Tuesday; 5lb wrong.

Three-time winner over hurdles; career highlight a win in Red Mills Auction Final at the 2025 Punchestown festival last year; has run creditably in good handicaps; staying on when falling three out at the Punchestown festival; outpaced from the last when fourth behind Putapoundinthejar at Bellewstown; 5lb wrong, good claimer.

RaceName: Book To Stay- Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Won over C&D (first-time visor) for Robert Cowell in March; beaten a short head on stable debut at Musselburgh (5f, good) last month, but failed to beat a rival at Ayr (5f, good to firm; blindfold removed late) ten days ago; needs to bounce back.

RaceName: Book To Stay- Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: 0-10 in handicaps since winning a Bath maiden (5.7f, soft) last September; second of ten at Kempton (6f, Polytrack) in April, but has gone quiet again on turf since; cheekpieces need to make a difference.

RaceName: Book To Stay- Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Not shown a great deal in three starts over 6f/7f on Tapeta/turf; needs the switch to a handicap and drop in trip to bring about improvement; stable looks to hold better prospects with Havin A Flyer.

RaceName: Book To Stay- Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Off the mark at the 21st attempt when making all to beat My Mate Mackley by just over a length at Southwell (5f, Tapeta) a week ago; 6lb worse off with the runner-up under penalty, but not dismissed now that she has got her head in front.

RaceName: Book To Stay- Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Off the mark at the eighth attempt here (6f) in March; not disgraced when fourth of ten over C&D last month but disappointed when sent off favourite at Leicester (5f, good) a week later; has undergone wind surgery since; needs to bounce back.

RaceName: Book To Stay- Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Has continued to run well (including in cheekpieces) since dead-heating on handicap debut at Chepstow (5f, good to soft) in May, including when staying on to be beaten just over a length behind Havin A Flyer at Southwell (5f, Tapeta) seven days ago; 6lb better off so has a good chance of being able to reverse the form.

RaceName: Book To Stay- Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Hooded all starts; well held in two outings for Jamie Osborne last August and again on stable debut at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month; half-sister to an AW winner, but needs plenty of improvement on handicap debut.

RaceName: Book To Stay- Wolverhampton Holiday Inn Handicap
Spotlight: Poor form in three starts including when beaten a long way into third of four on stable debut at Bath (5.7, firm) in May; possible she could improve now switched to a handicap, but it will very much be needed.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Last of three here in his penultimate race but successful either side of that, getting up close home on last week's nursery debut at Doncaster (extended 6f; good to firm; first-time blinkers); the penalty has to spell danger in this much deeper handicap.

Bang there in three of his four races (the last two over 7f) and he was only 5l away when 66-1 for the Coventry on his second start; likely to give his running once more, but he's probably vulnerable off this mark unless first-time cheekpieces can make a difference.

OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: All runs 7f on good or good to firm; comfortably won a Lingfield maiden before 66-1 in the Chesham at Royal Ascot and performing accordingly, so his Group 1 entry in Ireland looks optimistic; the stable's handicappers always need a second look here but he wouldn't be the obvious answer.

First two runs were over 6f and gelded after; took quite a strong hold at Sandown (7f, good) recently, so it's to his credit that he rallied for third, just behind Cilician; open to improvement in this bigger-field scenario, and David Evans appears to mean business in booking Colin Keane.

Narrowly repelled Cilician off level weights in a 6f novice at Nottingham in early June, after which he failed to fire in the Coventry at Royal Ascot; upped to 7f for nursery debut in a small field at Chester (good) and that race didn't go entirely to plan behind the winner who ran quite well in Listed race at Ascot last week; handily drawn and could have a part to play.

Made his debut over 5f and it was at 7f that he got off the mark in a small field at Haydock (good to soft); tackled 6f in the Woodcote at Epsom (good to soft) and finished to some effect to take fourth; returning to further can be beneficial and Ryan Moore has a good draw to work with.

Three runs over 6f in the north, last time at Newcastle (AW) where staying on the best to deny an odds-on Gosden inmate; looks ready for 7f, as pedigree would suggest with his dam a daughter of Galileo; enters the reckoning on handicap debut.

Unbeaten since upped to 6f and, although both races were sellers, the latest at York (won well) is always a strong race for the grade and connections retained his services for £30,000; stall 16 could pose problems but this colt is firmly on the upgrade and 7f could suit.

Both runs over 7f on good to firm; out of a 1m4f winner; looked nice when overcoming a slow start to win comfortably at Carlisle and he chased home respected opposition in a good time at Ascot (the winner Dr Rascal won Tuesday's Vintage Stakes); there's no doubt he has better to come and Oisin Murphy is often a significant booking for this yard.

Scopey colt who was all the better for being gelded when going down by a neck at Catterick (7f, good to soft; tried to make all) and the winner has since defied a penalty at Sandown, beating Cilician and My A'Ali Baba; shrewd trainer has secured Toby Moore's useful claim and stall 1 is ideal should he again go from the front; wears first-time blinkers.

All runs over 6f on good or faster ground; a Windsor winner in May but he suffered heavy defeats either side of that, latterly in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot (125-1); pedigree firmly points towards this trip suiting him better, but he isn't overly appealing with cheekpieces now turned to.

Her standout RPR came in the 7f maiden win at Doncaster last month (good to firm); however, she had no apparent excuses when behind The Ginger Kid on nursery debut at Chester and she's been dealt a wicked draw.
Beaten at Thirsk and Beverley (twice) at trips over about 7f and, unless transformed by a recent gelding operation, he'll do well to get involved from the widest stall.

Prominent racer who was too free in a 6f Newmarket novice in May and the cheekpieces enlisted there are swiftly removed; this initial mark looks on the high side even if he's judged on his Doncaster second the run before.

Came from well behind to win at Nottingham in May (6f, good) before outclassed in the Albany (100-1) at Royal Ascot; seemed to see out 7f fine when a close third of five in her first nursery at Lingfield (AW) but that was Class 5 and this race demands plenty more from her; wears first-time cheekpieces.

From last year's successful stable; bred for further but has improved with each run and was nicely on top late on when making all in a 7f maiden at Epsom one month ago (good); she'll do well to adopt the same tactics here from stall 14 but likely to finish her race off well.

Had considerable traffic issues when behind The Ginger Kid and Cilician on his debut but he hasn't kicked on from there, weakening last time at Newbury when raised to 7f (again behind Cilician); needs to be seen in a very different light if he's to feature on nursery debut.
Four starts (5f/6f); suffered interference when beating one home on his nursery debut at York (6f) but he was 28-1 and this race is no easier.

Won in first-time blinkers for William Haggas at Newcastle (6f) in January but she's not come close to that form in seven subsequent runs for two different yards; now 3lb lower than for her win but overall record is 1-13 and others are preferred; headgear removed.

13-race maiden who was well held at Wolverhampton (7f) two weeks ago but she went close over 6f there on her penultimate run; has claims if she can recapture that form and she's in the mix back in trip.

Seven-race maiden who has bled from the nose in her last three starts but she made some encouraging late headway when fourth at Redcar (6f, good) last month; continues to drop down the weights and has possibilities if she can find some extra spark.

Tailed off in his last two runs but he's a dual winner who bounced back when beating 13 rivals at Redcar (6f, good) in May; that form puts him in the picture and yard has won this race in last two years; not ruled out.
Won off 4lb higher at Chelmsford (6f, AW) in December but he's not easy to predict and has finished down the field in his last three starts; record is now 1-18 and others are more convincing,

Unexposed filly who found improvement when a front-running third in a Redcar handicap (6f, good) last month; finished ahead of Mereside Spark in that race and she's a big player if she can back that up.
Six-race maiden who has not finished closer than 6l to a winner including in three handicaps (5f-7f); mark has bottomed out now and she needs a transformation back on turf.
Has had issues at the start in all three runs and she's been beaten 13l or more in all of them; now goes handicapping with blinkers added but she needs lots of improvement after another break.

Four wins last year; fourth in this race last year; career best when winning a competitive fillies' handicap at Leopardstown in September; uneven form this season; most recent run, when second in a six-runner contest at the Curragh, gives her a fighting chance.
7f winner for Andre Fabre, has dropped to a more reasonable mark after four Irish starts; talented apprentice booked, but stable's other runner, Glyndwr, is more appealing.

High draw is a concern; however, holds a strong chance based on Killarney maiden win in May and an emphatic recent hurdles success at Cork; form of Killarney win has been shown in a good light by runner-up Treasure Rose in winning twice and finishing fifth in a Listed race.

Runner-up on five occasions; had become expensive to follow before beating Earls narrowly at Killarney, justifying good market support; has gone up 8lb, but his confidence may have been boosted by the breakthrough win.
Won for the second time when taking a 1m Leopardstown handicap on return; three unplaced runs since then; lame on penultimate start.

OwnerName: Thomas J O'Connor & Ms Hazel McGuinness
Spotlight: Nine wins in all, but only one on turf from 32 starts; fair third over 7f at Fairyhouse on his penultimate start; last of six on most recent outing.

Three-time AW winner for Ger Lyons; in good form last October/November; has been a high price on all four starts for this stable; should enter calculations now after showing a revival of form in two Leopardstown races.

Durable handicapper with 11 wins to his name, the latest being on his favoured soft ground at Roscommon last September; has notched three consecutive seconds since May; concerning that he has been unplaced in seven Galway attempts.

Three wins in Britain in 2023 at up to 1m; regressive in 2024 and 2025 seasons; produced best run for some time at Dundalk in March when good second over 1m; after three more runs, took advantage of a drop in grade when winning a claimer at Limerick; backed that up in a Ballinrobe handicap; was 4lb wrong when ninth in the big handicap here on Tuesday.
Placed in three consecutive 1m handicaps lately; closely matched with No More Porter on Gowran running five days ago; missed an engagement on Tuesday.
Won a Dundalk maiden on debut in January 2025; weak turf form after long absence; has slumped in the ratings; perhaps worth a market check.

All three wins have been gained at the Curragh and a large portion of his places too; good second over 1m at his favoured venue last month; has continued in good form with placed efforts at Killarney and Gowran.
Rated 84 at her peak; weak form this season but could be of interest now off a reduced mark (72); cheekpieces added to usual tongue-tie.
Narrowly denied at Gowran in June only two days after Limerick win; well beaten in the race in which San Aer finished second here on Tuesday.

Has two C&D wins to his name, and finished second to the smart Ribee at this venue last October; fair run at Killarney in the middle of the month; 11-4 when narrowly denied here on Tuesday; obvious chance of this does not come too soon.
AW and turf winner; 12lb higher than for her turf win; a staying-on seventh in the 8.15 on Tuesday; held by San Aer on that running.

In good form on turf, including two wins, before disappointing when sent off favourite at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) this month; may not have handled the ground there but he didn't show much in one previous go on the AW (over 7f here) and is drawn wide, so does have a bit to prove.
Twice well beaten off this mark since winning narrowly at Lingfield (1m, Polytrack) last month; can blow the start; blinkers return, but risky.

Ended a lengthy losing run at Newcastle (1m4f, Tapeta) in January but disappointed when favourite back there (1m2f) later in month; no headgear on this return from 191 days off and this trip looks on the sharp side.
0-7; not beaten far into sixth of 13 at Southwell (7f, Tapeta) a week ago and drops in grade; still has something to prove back up in trip.

11-time AW winner, the latest a Newcastle seller for the Moores (1m, Tapeta) last October; regressive for this yard in the meantime despite plummeting in the weights; best watched unless the market suggests otherwise.
Two of his three wins have come here (9.5f/7f), the latest in March; ran with credit when fourth of ten at Lingfield (7f, Polytrack) last time and he makes the shortlist.

Made a successful stable debut over C&D in September 2024 and, having dropped 1lb lower than for that win, was scoring for the first time since when just getting up at Kempton (1m, Polytrack) this month; back up 3lb but respected nonetheless.
Unplaced in seven starts for Archie Watson last year; changed hands for 4,000gns in October and now makes her debut for new yard after ten months off; watch the market.

Course regular who won over 7f in March; only 2lb higher and mainly running well in the meantime but, although she has run with credit over this far, there's a suspicion that a shorter trip suits her better.

Showed some promise in three outings for the Crisfords as a 2yo, but little in five starts for this yard since returning from a long absence in December; switch to a visor will need to make a big difference.

Has failed to beat a rival in his last two starts here, the latest on his return from 144 days off this month; however, he was in fine form on the AW in midwinter prior to those below-par efforts,  winning twice over C&D; may be worth chancing and market support would be interesting.

OwnerName: Dr M Voikhansky & Mrs S Voikhanskaya
Spotlight: Placed in both previous goes over C&D but is now 0-21; needs something extra starting out for another new yard (same owners).

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: By Masar out of smart 1m2f-1m4f winner; has made a bright start to her career with minor honours at Newbury (good to firm) over 6.5f and 6f, finishing well last time after jockey lost an iron; just about sets the form standard and, although better will surely be needed, could produce another big run.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 72,000gns yearling by Make Believe; first foal; dam 1m1f/1m4f winner (RPR 97), half-sister to 1m/9.5f Group 2 winner Military Law, out of 1m Group 3 winner; from a top yard, so needs a close look.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 115,000gns breeze-up 2yo by Blue Point; 9-2 for novice at Kempton (6f, AW) three weeks ago, coming from towards rear for third of nine; found her stride in good style late on, so could be a significant improver.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 30,000euros foal, £40,000 yearling, 62,000gns breeze-up 2yo by Starspangledbanner; sixth foal; half-sister to Italian 1m1f/1m3f winner Aretino; dam unplaced at 1m (RPR 65), sister to bumper and useful 2m-2m3f hurdle/chase winner Stamp Your Feet, half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Memory; hooded for debut; yard had a newcomer win at this meeting in 2017.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 35,000gns half-sister to winners including Grocer Jack (1m2f/10.5f including German/Italian Group 3; RPR 116); 12-1, green when beaten nearly 9l in novice at Newmarket (5f, good to firm) in early May; needs big improvement with the hood enlisted.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Showcasing close relation to 5f winner Fashion Queen (including 2yo/Listed; RPR 106); second favourite, kept on well from off the pace when second of eight in novice at York (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; firmly in the mix among those who have run.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Eighth foal; Sea The Moon half-sister to six winners including Notation (1m-2m AW, including KSA; RPR 102), Temporize (1m4f-2m4f; 98) and Cool Party (8.5f-2m including 2yo; 97); dam 1m4f-1m6f winner (98); late foal; newcomer for trainer who also runs Donna Beauty and the market can give clues.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Third foal; Harry Angel half-sister to 6f AW winner Iconic Times (including 2yo; RPR 79); dam runner-up at 6f (63), half-sister to fairly useful winners, out of 7f winner; her trainer's first 2yo runner this term.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 160,000euros yearling by Wootton Bassett; second foal; dam US 6f turf winner, half-sister to winners Guildsman (US 6.5f Grade 3) and La Galiote (French 7.5f/1m), out of maiden half-sister to dam of 1m2f/10.5f Group 1 winner Almanzor; worth a second look for yard whose 2yos are doing well.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 35,000gns foal, 52,000gns yearling; fourth foal; Pinatubo half-sister to winners Live Each Day (7f-1m3f; RPR 74), Fermain (6f 2yo; 70) and Grand Oak (US 5f turf including 2yo); dam 5.5f-7f winner (including 2yo) out of 6f 2yo Listed winner; trainer had two 2yo winners (with experience) on Monday.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: By Time Test; second foal; dam 1m3f winner (RPR 76), out of maiden half-sister to French 1m2f Group 1 winners Vadawina and Vazira; trainer off the mark with his 2026 juveniles last week.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 180,000gns yearling, 600,000euros breeze-up 2yo by Night Of Thunder; first foal; dam 1m2f winner (RPR 80), closely related to 1m Listed winner Token Of Love (dam of 7f/1m Group 3 winner Mighty Ulysses), out of Listed-placed half-sister to 1m Group 1 winner Rebecca Sharp; major yard had two good 2yo winners at Ascot last week, so market strength should be a big pointer.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: By Wootton Bassett, while dam Love won on her third start as 2yo before going on to take the Group 1 Moyglare as 2yo and complete the 1,000 Guineas/Oaks double; weak 6-1 for maiden at Leopardstown (1m, good) two weeks ago and ran on well from the back for second of six; has her own Moyglare entry for top connections and their runners tend to improve markedly.

RaceName: Tatler British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 90,000euros yearling by State Of Rest; third foal; half-sister to winners Sounds Like A Plan (6f-1m including 2yo/HK; RPR 95) and Reprised (6f AW; 80); dam 5f 2yo winner (including Listed; 98) out of 1m Listed winner; from an in-form stable which had 2yo wins (their first of the season) last Friday and Saturday.

RaceName: oddschecker.com AJA Novice Amateur Jockeys' Handicap (Riders With 3 Wins Or Less At Start Of Season)
Spotlight: Has form figures of 14323112253 since Boxing Day and that latest third was a good effort from a wide draw at Wolverhampton; still looks on a workable mark and he's respected in suitable conditions back on turf; yard also runs Palazzo Persico.

RaceName: oddschecker.com AJA Novice Amateur Jockeys' Handicap (Riders With 3 Wins Or Less At Start Of Season)
Spotlight: Admirable veteran who recorded his 15th turf win when battling well to score at Ripon (1m2f, good) 12 days ago; that was his third success from his last seven starts and he's a big player again off only 2lb higher here.

RaceName: oddschecker.com AJA Novice Amateur Jockeys' Handicap (Riders With 3 Wins Or Less At Start Of Season)
Spotlight: Turned things around with a win at Redcar (1m, good) last month and he's held his form with placed efforts in both runs since; hard to rule out another good run but he looks weighted near best off this mark and is untried at this trip.

RaceName: oddschecker.com AJA Novice Amateur Jockeys' Handicap (Riders With 3 Wins Or Less At Start Of Season)
OwnerName: Old Gold Racing, Tim Cottier & Partner
Spotlight: Well handicapped on his best form at up to 1m2f last season but he's still a maiden after 11 starts and has finished seventh in both runs this year; has bit to prove after another break and others are preferred.

RaceName: oddschecker.com AJA Novice Amateur Jockeys' Handicap (Riders With 3 Wins Or Less At Start Of Season)
Spotlight: His last Flat win was over two years ago and he was tailed off on his stable debut at Wolverhampton (1m6f) last week; has plenty to prove and he needs a major revival back in trip; tongue-tie removed.

RaceName: oddschecker.com AJA Novice Amateur Jockeys' Handicap (Riders With 3 Wins Or Less At Start Of Season)
Spotlight: Six-time winner split between AW and turf; has mixed record since his last success in February but he was only just caught at Windsor (1m, good to firm) last time; has possibilities if he can back that up and he has won over this trip.
Without a win since 2024 but earns good marks for his consistency in recent months and lost out only by a head off today's mark at Ripon (1m2f, good) in June; probably won't be far away.

Best known as a Brighton specialist but also runs this track well; needs to rebound from disappointing C&D run four weeks ago but looked in good nick when scoring at Brighton (1m2f, good to firm) in June; shortlisted.

OwnerName: W Trenchard, A Coupland, Cheam Marketng
Spotlight: Scored over 8.5f here (good) last summer and kept on for respectable fourth at Brighton (1m4f, good to firm) on latest Flat start in May; returns to this code on a workable mark and after a recent second over hurdles; likely contender.

Not far off career-best form when coming from the rear for clearcut success at Bath (1m2f, firm) in May but not seen to same effect on either subsequent outing; chance may depend upon others setting a strong pace.
Managed only fifth of eight when upped to 1m2f at Windsor (good to firm) two months ago and remains without a win since 2023; continues to edge down the weights but needs to turn a corner.
Placed off 3lb higher at Lingfield (1m2f, good) on seasonal/stable debut in May but not quite in same form on any of three subsequent outings, the last twice here (1m2f/8.5f); needs to up his game.

Ground-versatile sort has hit form lately, winning over 1m2f at Navan and carrying a 7lb penalty at Killarney over just short of this trip; up another 4lb but has run well in defeat at this track and looks a player.
Dual-purpose sort has been soundly beaten on recent Flat runs but ran a cracker over hurdles at Bellewstown last time; chance if converting that back to this sphere.
Third runner for yard; runner-up at Gowran (9.5f) and Ballinrobe (1m5f) early in the season but her last three runs have been well below that level so needs a return to best.
Regressive over hurdles lately and Flat maiden hasn't run in this sphere for over three years; others preferred.

Winner in UK over 1m2f and best run for this yard came over that trip at Dundalk; not as good over 1m4f at Tramore but can be sharper for that run and do better; non-runner in the 8.15 here on Tuesday.

OwnerName: Conor O'Connor & Colum Currie & Mark Devenny
Spotlight: Broke her maiden over 1m as a 2yo here in heavy ground but no win since; tried over hurdles recently without success but some decent efforts; not ruled out.
Won his third race on AW when scoring over this trip last time; 5lb higher and needs to do more to break his turf duck.

OwnerName: D O'Mahony & D McHugh & D J Kelly & G Butler
Spotlight: Won over hurdles at Down Royal in May but was poor in soft ground last time; Flat maiden ran well enough in defeat here as a 2yo and has a shout on his best form.
Course winner over 7f in 2022 has run well in defeat back here since over 1m; similar efforts last three runs including up to an extended 1m3f; needs more; tough draw.
Dual-purpose winner has been soundly beaten on his last two Flat starts but has a chance on his Dundalk sixth last December.

One of his five wins came over 7f at this track in 2024; lost his form at the end of last year, and this trip is new; encouraging display when sixth of 17 (Dark Summit, eighth) over a shorter trip here on Tuesday.
Has shown some ability in maidens over various trips without progressing; raised in trip for handicap debut and not without a chance.
Won over 1m3f at Down Royal last year and 9.5f at Gowran last month; not bad runs twice since but needs more off this mark.
UK-trained; three of her four wins in UK have come on AW up to this trip; has dropped in the weights in the last year and solid runs in defeat lately; needs a bit more.
Maiden has shown some ability in defeat but has to improve hugely from her poor return at Roscommon when beaten 24l.
Maiden had been consistent enough in defeat until a poor run as fav' at Tramore last time so has to rebound with a tongue-tie added.

OwnerName: Annus Mirabilis Synd'/Sean O'Driscoll/Middle Cow Unlimited
Spotlight: Got off the mark over 9.5f at Ballinrobe and followed up over 1m3f at Naas when she wandered late on; is up 9lb for that but is improving rapidly and is on the shortlist from a low draw.
160,000gns yearling; has been off since finishing a well-held fifth of seven on his Newmarket debut (1m, good; 40-1) last October; may not come into his own until handicapping.

Brother to winners Samburu (7f/8.5f including 2yo/US; RPR 105), Fingerpaint (Group-placed 7f; 100) and Settlement (7f AW; 83); dam 7f 2yo winner (89), sister to US 8.5f Grade 2 winner Set Piece, half-sister to 6f/6.5f Listed winner Alocasia; any market support on debut would be significant.
Sent off 150-1 when a well-beaten sixth of seven on last month's Leicester debut (1m, good); may be one for handicaps in due course.

780,000euros yearling; half-sister to 1m4f winner Caspi Star (RPR 95); dam 9.7f/1m2f winner (including Listed; 105), half-sister to useful 12.5f winner Tashi, out of 5f winning half-sister to useful 1m-1m2f winner Al Galayel; plenty to like on breeding and the market should be revealing.

Made a promising return/stable debut when beaten a neck at Haydock (1m, good to firm) in April, but hasn't really built on it in two outings since; still respected on this switch to the AW if resuming her progress.
Showed a little ability on the AW at the start of the year but it would be surprising if she proved good enough in this field after 166 days off; hood given a go.

100,000euros yearling; sister to three winners including Indian Wish (1m/9.4f including AW/Listed; RPR 111) and Ashana (German 10.5f Listed; 98), half-sister to five winners including Incampo (French 6.7f-1m4f including 2yo; 103); dam 5.5f-7f winner (including German Listed; 100); attractive pedigree and sire 5-17 (29%) here in the past five seasons but the stable only has the occasional winner first time out; market useful.

OwnerName: Gestuet Schlenderhan Gmbh U Co Kg
Spotlight: Dam German 1m3f winner (Group 3; RPR 106), sent off 18-1 when an eyecatching fifth of 12 on her Southwell debut (7f, Tapeta) a week ago; bred to relish the longer trip and any improvement from that first outing would put her right in the mix.

Won in France last autumn on his two 2yo starts (6.5f/1m, soft/very soft); however, soundly beaten in an AW conditions race and Royal Ascot handicap on his two outings this year and he needs to raise his game.

Built upon 2yo promise to win big-field maiden at Newbury (1m, good) on reappearance and when 13th of 30 in the Britannia at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) he was third of 15 in the far-side group; possible player.

Fast-ground 2yo novice winner who reappeared with good second in a handicap at Musselburgh (1m, good to soft) in April; however, two lesser runs have followed; gelded since and has to get back on track.

4-4 in handicaps (1m/7f) prior to clear second to thriving winner at Carlisle (1m, good to firm) in May; disappointing at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago in first-time cheekpieces (retained) and something to prove on the back of that, but not written off in view of previous form.

9l maiden win at Lingfield (7f, AW) last November and reappeared with close Listed fourth there (7f) in February; he's dropped down the weights but his turf form on his last four starts hasn't come up to scratch.

Progressive this term and he got off the mark at Sandown (1m, good) in May on his second handicap start; couldn't quite get there when second of five at Sandown (1m1f, good) since but the expected competitive gallop in this big field should be right up his street, and he's one to consider.

Won both 2yo starts and, having been gelded, he returned to form when keeping on for fourth of 14 at York (1m, good) last month; retains potential for top yard and the first-time cheekpieces could elicit something extra.

He's got better with each of this year's three runs and he got back on the scoresheet when making all with something to spare at Carlisle (1m, good to firm) last month; 6lb higher in a tougher race today but this progressive colt could make another bold bid.

Made debut in April and he improved upon his first two runs when winning by a short head at Leicester (1m, good) last month; he's not obviously well treated off his opening mark but he cost 475,000gns as a yearling and is in good hands to continue to progress; Oisin Murphy has an excellent record for the yard in the last five seasons (18-39; 46%).

Reappeared with a win at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) in April and he followed up on his handicap debut at Newbury (1m, good); represents in-form yard and he's probably capable of better than he showed when sixth of ten over C&D (good) last month, but others arrive with more pressing claims.

Won Kempton maiden (1m, AW) in April on fourth start then finished fifth on handicap debut at Haydock (1m, good to firm); gelded prior to winning four-runner handicap at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) a fortnight ago; up in grade and needs to prove he's fully effective on turf, but he's from a fine family and represents a top yard; respected in first-time cheekpieces.

He's finished in the first three on all four starts and was stretched by 1m2f when turned over at odds-on last time; wears first-time cheekpieces on handicap debut and his stable won this in 2023; Ryan Moore rides and improvement is possible, but necessary if he's to defy his opening mark.

Close third over C&D in June on second handicap start (good; Get Outta Here second) and filled the same position at Ascot (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago, albeit no match for the first two; he might have an each-way shout in first-time cheekpieces.

Won at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm) in June and at Southwell (1m, AW) on July 5; did well to finish third at Windsor (1m, good to firm) last time having hung badly left, which he also did when winning there; it remains to be seen how he'll cope with the camber in the straight at this tricky track, but he has plenty of ability provided it's harnessed in the right direction.

Twice finished third behind Law Court and The Joker at Sandown (1m/1m1f, good) then finished fourth of eight there (1m2f, good to firm); he's raced ten times, with one win, and improvement is needed in this hot contest.

Won on handicap debut at Lingfield (7.6f, good to firm) in May then went very close over this C&D (good) where he had to wait for a run; made good headway from the rear before his effort flattened out at York (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago, finishing third; could have a part to play.

He's raced in four handicaps this year and has twice made the frame (7f/1m, good/good to firm); however, he was well beaten at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago and needs to bounce back with a career-best effort.

Won at Kempton (7f, AW) last November on sole 2yo start; fifth on both outings this season, most recently on handicap debut at Windsor (1m, good to firm) when beaten 3l; very lightly raced and improvement can't be ruled out, but he certainly needs to take a step forward today.

OwnerName: Two Plus Three Two Plus Four
Spotlight: He's yet to pose a serious threat this season but has run some respectable races, as when keeping on from the rear for fifth at Ascot (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago; edging down the weights and this big-field scenario and expected strong pace could see him to good effect; interesting.

RaceName: Spillers EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

RaceName: Spillers EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

RaceName: Spillers EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Well beaten over C&D (good) on debut at start of this month and didn't achieve much when last of five at Nottingham (6f, good to firm) a fortnight ago.

RaceName: Spillers EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Showed fair form when placed at Nottingham (6f, good to firm) last month, his third start, and has plenty of scope for improvement over this longer trip but he's not straightforward and might still be a work in progress.

RaceName: Spillers EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Posed no threat on her debut but was seemingly in process of faring better before stumble 2f out cost her momentum over C&D (good to firm) three weeks ago; remains tricky to weigh up but could have a say.

RaceName: Spillers EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Never better than midfield when 50-1 for debut at Newbury (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; probably one for further down the line.
Tailed-off on recent debut at Ballinrobe and can't be fancied on that evidence.
Finished in the frame in three of five point starts; will have to do a fair bit more on bumper debut.
Pulled-up in both point starts but some promise on bumper debut at Listowel; will have to improve plenty from that.
One of two runners for yard; well-bred sort was runner-up on his third point start and ran respectably on bumper debut at Punchestown; tongue-tie added and has to improve a fair bit.
Comes from a decent pedigree; ran with credit on debut at Punchestown behind an impressive winner; the hood worn then is retained and should be more closely involved with improvement to come.
His two best runs came on debut at Fairyhouse last November and at Listowel (2m4f) last time; the cheekpieces worn then are retained and this 2f drop in trip should be fine; chance.
Little promise in points, a hurdle and this bumper last year so is passed over today.
Beaten 38l on debut at Ballinrobe and will have to improve loads on that for a local trainer.
A fine debut run at Punchestown last year but was tailed off next time there; questions back after a long lay-off.

Ran a cracker when just denied on second point start back in May; bought by current connections for 80,000GBP after; leading amateur retains the ride and is one to consider, especially if market strength behind him.

Half-brother to winners Kilbarry Chianti (2m3f hurdle), Kilbarry Lilly (2m4f hurdle) and Kilbarry Classic (bumper); dam unraced half-sister to winners incl' Tropical Lady (1m2f Group 2); from a fine family but made only E4,000 as a foal then realised E45,000  as a 3yo; maximum respect from this source.
Similar efforts in defeat in two bumpers, at Punchestown and Bellewstown; got wound up before the start last time and that is a concern here; shouldn't be far away if running his race.
Ran a solid race on debut at Punchestown when just behind Sir Vinnie and Monday's bumper runner-up here Which Flannerys (stablemate); ran green then so can go close if more switched on now.
Third on sole point run and posted similar efforts in defeat in bumpers at Downpatrick and Killarney; should be involved again but needs to find more to score.

Second runner for yard; half-brother to winners Blakey Boy (2m4f-3m2f hurdle/chase) and Knocknagoran Lady (2m6f/3m1f hurdle); dam from the family of Grand National winner Rule The World; E2,000 vendor buyback as a 3yo; seems one to just watch on debut.
Second runner for yard; beaten 20l on sole point start but the winner looks smart and went on to make 290,000GBP at the sales; the market may be a guide to expectations.
Beaten 25l on debut at Cork last month and will have to improve loads from that.

RaceName: Free Bets On attheraces.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C & D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: By Due Diligence; second foal; brother to 6f/7f 2yo winner Glitterati (RPR 91); unraced dam out of maiden half-sister to useful winners Audience (7f/1m) and Pacific Pride (5f/6f); gelded newcomer for whom the market should guide, with yard also running Ouragan.

RaceName: Free Bets On attheraces.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C & D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 100-1, weakened to go down by 23l in a novice at Newbury (6f, good to firm) three weeks ago; steps down in class.

RaceName: Free Bets On attheraces.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C & D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: By Land Force; first foal; dam placed at 1m6f-2m AW (RPR 65), out of French 1m5f winning half-sister to 6f Group 1 winner Librisa Breeze; stable's first 2yo runner this season was due at Goodwood 5.20.

RaceName: Free Bets On attheraces.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C & D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 33-1, came from the rear when just over 5l sixth of ten in maiden at Bath (5f, good) in early May; should improve but needs to in a major way.

RaceName: Free Bets On attheraces.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C & D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Ran twice at Nottingham (6f, good to firm) this summer, when racing freely on debut but much improved (leading 4f) for second of five to a red-hot favourite 13 days ago; stable runs two; bold show is likely from stall 1.

RaceName: Free Bets On attheraces.com EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C & D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB Race)
